&reftitle.description;
public boolSQLite3::busyTimeout intmilliseconds
Sets a busy handler that will sleep until the database is not locked or the timeout is reached.
The busy handler is built into SQLite, so no callback has to be provided. When a statement finds the database locked by another connection, SQLite keeps retrying for up to milliseconds. If the database is still locked after that, the statement fails with a database is locked error (SQLITE_BUSY).
How that failure shows up depends on SQLite3::enableExceptions. With exceptions enabled, an SQLite3Exception is thrown. Otherwise an E_WARNING is raised and the method that ran the statement, such as SQLite3::exec or SQLite3::query, returns &false;.
By default no busy handler is set, so a statement fails right away if the database is locked.

&reftitle.returnvalues;
Returns &true; if the busy timeout was set, &return.falseforfailure;. The return value only tells whether the timeout was set. It does not mean that later statements will get the lock in time.
